---
title: "Fit a linear model and predict"
---

Fit monthly rent from floor area and district, then predict the rent of two new flats with 95% prediction intervals.

The example runs with the phit extension or the plain-PHP polyfill ([Extension or polyfill](../extension-or-polyfill.qmd)). The data are ten simulated flats: `rent` is the monthly rent in an unnamed currency, `area` is the floor area in square meters, and `district` is one of three districts.

## Code

```php
use function Phit\{fit_ols, predict};

$flats = [
    'rent' => [
        1879.25, 1805.03, 2022.29, 1267.85, 1509.24,
        2240.10, 959.51, 2386.54, 1655.80, 1420.00,
    ],
    'area' => [
        74.4, 57.4, 66.4, 49.1, 45.7,
        92.4, 37.0, 93.9, 61.2, 52.3,
    ],
    'district' => [
        'north', 'south', 'north', 'east', 'south',
        'north', 'east', 'south', 'east', 'south',
    ],
];

$fit = fit_ols('rent ~ area + district', $flats);

foreach ($fit['columns'] as $i => $name) {
    printf(
        "%-14s %8.2f  95%% CI [%8.2f, %8.2f]\n",
        $name,
        $fit['coefficients'][$i],
        ...$fit['conf_int'][$i],
    );
}
printf(
    "R-squared %.3f, residual SD %.2f\n\n",
    $fit['r_squared'],
    $fit['sigma'],
);

$new = [
    'area' => [50.0, 80.0],
    'district' => ['east', 'north'],
];
$p = predict($fit, $new, interval: 'prediction');

foreach ($p['fit'] as $i => $rent) {
    printf(
        "%.0f m2, %-5s %8.2f  95%% PI [%7.2f, %7.2f]\n",
        $new['area'][$i],
        $new['district'][$i],
        $rent,
        $p['lower'][$i],
        $p['upper'][$i],
    );
}
```

## Output

```
(Intercept)      352.64  95% CI [  -87.49,   792.77]
area              19.18  95% CI [   11.27,    27.09]
districtnorth    203.64  95% CI [ -166.19,   573.47]
districtsouth    232.16  95% CI [  -60.58,   524.90]
R-squared 0.927, residual SD 146.29

50 m2, east   1311.65  95% PI [ 898.26, 1725.04]
80 m2, north  2090.69  95% PI [1676.97, 2504.41]
```

## Interpretation

- `district` becomes a factor. Its first level alphabetically, `east`, is the reference.
- Each district coefficient compares that district with `east` for flats of the same area.
- The `area` coefficient is an association within districts, not the effect of enlarging a flat.
- Ten flats give wide intervals, so the district differences are uncertain.
- A prediction interval covers one new flat's rent. A confidence interval (`interval: 'confidence'`) covers the mean rent and is narrower.
